Significantly higher scores in one or more psychological distress states were found for females, and those not in a relationship, in the lowest income category, aged 18–45 years, or with a chronic illness.
Eligible participants included all Australian adults aged 18 years and over.
Response options were “Never”, “Monthly or less”, “2–4 times a month”, “2–3 times a week”, and “4 or more times a week”.
In total, 1491 people (mean age 50.5 ± 14.9 years, 999 female) completed the survey.
The average physical activity of participants was 312.5 minutes/week, but almost half ( n = 729, 48.9%) reported a reduction in physical activity since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The average sleep duration reported prior to the onset of COVID-19 was 7.1 ± 1.3 h per night, with half ( n = 756, 50.7%) reporting no change in sleep quality since COVID-19.
